clue.text: It can be dark in bars

definitions.text: It can be dark in bars

parts.words: It can be dark in bars
parts.note: reads like something gloomy in pubs or prisons, but the bars are slabs of confectionery and dark describes a cocoa-rich kind

explanation.surface: Something shadowy lurks in pubs or behind prison bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs or a jail cell; here they are slabs of sweets, and 'dark' is the bitter, milk-free variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark, milk-free confection is sold in bars, so this is a cryptic description of it.

clue.text: One can't recall having it

parts.note: reads as a lapse about owning something, but describes the condition of memory loss itself

explanation.surface: Someone cannot remember ever owning a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests forgetting a possession; the joke is that the condition is the forgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory loss is a medical condition whose sufferer cannot remember things, including having it.

clue.text: The name is French for a cosy place

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
the French word for 'is' is est

explanation.surface: A French word for a snug spot is being explained.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's snug home of twigs is the model for any cosy retreat.

clue.text: He has this done, possibly, just for pleasure

definitions.text: He has this done, possibly, just for pleasure

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A man gets something done purely because he enjoys it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THIS DONE; the whole clue also describes the answer, a man who acts only for enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker lives for enjoyment, doing things only because they gratify him.

clue.text: Touch-type?

parts.note: looks like keyboard skill, but touch is slang for asking someone for money, and type means a kind of person

explanation.surface: A question about typing without looking at the keys.
explanation.walkthrough: To touch someone for money is British slang for scrounging from them; the clue asks for the type of person who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger habitually begs small loans or favours, which is touching people for cash.

clue.text: Middle-gear selections?

parts.note: suggests choosing a car's middle gears, but means garments worn around the middle of the body

explanation.surface: A driver picks third or fourth gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' reads as a car's gearbox but means clothing; the middle is the waist and groin.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple cloths wrapped about the waist are clothing for the body's middle.

clue.text: They are found in dens, often-and this includes the first lady!

definitions.text: They are found in dens, often

indicators.note: includes means the word this holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: Creatures living in lairs, apparently including the very first woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first lady' is not a president's wife but Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbers traditionally gather in a den of iniquity, a crooks' hideout.

clue.text: I take prim poetry to replace such bad taste

indicators.note: read as re-place, to put the letters of I with prim poetry in new positions

explanation.surface: Someone swaps dull, prissy verse for something showing poor judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' is read as re-place: the letters of I and PRIM POETRY are set in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly behaviour shows a lack of decorum, which is a failing of taste.

clue.text: No deed is prepared to be so inequitable

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working the letters of no deed into a new order

explanation.surface: No act is ready to be unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment favours only one party, so it is biased to a single camp.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, I would visit the Isle of Man

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone says, so to speak, that they'd go to the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression peculiar to a language is a characteristic way of saying something.

clue.text: Fare forced into a banger?

parts.note: suggests passengers crammed into an old car, but describes minced filling pushed into a sausage skin

explanation.surface: Passengers are crammed into a clapped-out old car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is both a ramshackle car and a sausage; 'fare' is food, not a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned minced pork is the stuffing packed into skins to make links.

clue.text: It is found as well in alluvial soils

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run alluvial soils

explanation.surface: Something is present too in river-deposited earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Too, besides and additionally are synonyms for this adverb.

clue.text: Intelligence of an agent protected by insurance

definitions.meaning: secret work by a spy operating in disguise
having a policy in force, beneath its protection

explanation.surface: A spy's information is safeguarded by an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies working in secret are said to operate this way, and a policy in force places goods beneath its protection.

clue.text: Tight budget upsets one's rights

indicators.note: upsets means knocks over, so the letters of one's rights are disordered

explanation.surface: Being short of money annoys a person who feels entitled.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on very little money is the idiom for running things with minimal funds.

clue.text: A box of tar?

parts.note: suggests a crate of pitch, but tar is crossword slang for a sailor and the box is his trunk

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a container of pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' (short for tarpaulin) is old slang for a sailor; the box is the trunk a seaman keeps his belongings in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner stores his kit in a wooden trunk aboard ship.

clue.text: Pitch out of bed? It's a close thing!

parts.note: to pitch is to throw or toss
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Throwing someone out of bed turns into a near-run contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest whose outcome is evenly balanced is as uncertain as flipping a coin.

clue.text: To make a list is not permitted, after hours

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: Drawing up a list is forbidden once the hour is late.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange data in columns or rows is to set it out as an orderly list.

clue.text: Maxims of international bankers from Zurich?

definitions.meaning: the Swiss financiers nicknamed after small earth-dwelling creatures of folklore

explanation.surface: The sayings of Swiss financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s British jibe at Swiss bankers thought to speculate against the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphorisms are also called by this word, and Swiss financiers were dubbed after goblin-like folklore figures.

clue.text: Sketch of old hat with band

parts.note: something old hat is out of fashion, or out
a band or stripe is a line

explanation.surface: A drawing of an antique hat with a ribbon round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing showing only the main contours is a basic sketch.

clue.text: I mark his bad language!

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters of I mark his are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A teacher grades someone's poor use of words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the tongue spoken in the Himalayan region between India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Base soldier returns before August!

indicators.note: returns means the soldier's letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
august means dignified or noble

explanation.surface: A lowly soldier comes back home before the summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' is capitalised to look like the month; it is the adjective meaning grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and dishonourable conduct is the opposite of high-minded.

clue.text: Standing commendation

explanation.surface: Praise while on one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Good repute is one sense, and acknowledgement or praise, as in giving someone their due, is another.

clue.text: Foot-long skeleton from Sumatra, set out

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of Sumatra set are laid in a new order

explanation.surface: A twelve-inch skeleton is displayed, brought from an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot-long' is not twelve inches: it is the skeleton running along the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of bones between ankle and toes forms the framework of the foot.

clue.text: Can University put back assembly?

indicators.note: put back means the two pieces are written in reverse order

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Can a college postpone its meeting?
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained component or assembled group functions as a single item.

clue.text: Girl who made Wordsworth's heart leap up?

definitions.text: who made Wordsworth's heart leap up?
definitions.meaning: Wordsworth wrote that his heart leaps up when he beholds a rainbow, and the Greek goddess of the rainbow bears this name

explanation.surface: A woman who thrilled the poet Wordsworth.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is 'My heart leaps up when I behold / A rainbow in the sky'; the rainbow goddess is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female forename and also the name of the Greek goddess personifying the rainbow.

clue.text: A party, I claim in court

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: Someone makes a statement before a judge at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's plea of having been elsewhere is a claim made at trial.

clue.text: Help to turn people with a stream of abuse

indicators.note: to turn means the helping word is read in reverse

parts.note: help is aid
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: Assistance for converting a community comes with torrents of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter, sustained verbal attack is a torrent of invective.

clue.text: There is no gravity in this physical condition

definitions.text: There is no gravity in this physical condition

parts.words: There is no gravity in this physical condition
parts.note: reads as a state lacking seriousness, but gravity is the physical pull that makes things heavy

explanation.surface: A bodily state in which nothing is taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' seems to mean solemnity, but it is the force giving mass its heft, as for astronauts in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts in orbit feel no pull of the earth, so they float freely.
